title: Inference Caching and Residual Data Handling Addendum (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This addendum language is intended to be attached to customer agreements (DPA or MSA) to address obligations, SLAs and evidentiary expectations specific to inference-time caching and transient data produced, processed, or stored by the inference runtime (e.g., prefix/KV caches, prompt/response caches, blob caches). It is focused on residual data exposure risk, auditability, and operational commitments for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies to any managed or customer-deployed inference environment where live request handling may create transient or semi-persistent artifacts (KV caches, prefix caches, request caches, debug traces, local temp files).
- Not a replacement for the core DPA. Intended to be a narrowly scoped addendum covering caching behaviors, retention windows, evidence, and SLA commitments tied to residual data.

Key Definitions (for contracting):
- Residual Data: Any data derived from or containing customer-provided inputs or model outputs that persists in any runtime cache, temporary storage, or logs after the inference request completes.
- KV Cache: Key-value cache used to store intermediate transformer state (attention keys/values) for caching of repeated prefixes or session contexts.
- Ephemeral Cache: Memory-backed or transient-on-disk caches intended to be cleared on process exit or on an eviction schedule.
- Persisted Artifact: Any file or object written to disk, object storage, or a database that survives service restarts without explicit purge actions.

Contractual Obligations (draft clauses):
1) Data Minimization and Segregation:
  - Provider shall not persist customer-provided or customer-derived data in any persisted artifact unless expressly configured by the customer or required for legal/regulatory reasons.
  - Runtime shall separate KV/ephemeral caches by tenant/organization id. Multi-tenant hosting will not reuse cache buckets across tenants.

2) Retention and Automatic Purge Windows:
  - Ephemeral caches: cleared within 15 minutes of session termination or as soon as memory pressure requires eviction, unless explicitly pinned by customer configuration.
  - KV caches used for session resumption: default TTL 24 hours; customer may request shorter TTLs or per-tenant immediate eviction.
  - Persistent debug or trace artifacts: retention no longer than 30 days unless customer opts in for extended retention for debugging; access restricted to named roles.

3) Explicit Customer Controls and Operational APIs:
  - Provider will expose APIs or console actions for: immediate per-tenant cache purge, scheduled purge configuration, and export of cache metadata without payloads (e.g., cache keys, sizes, timestamps).
  - For private/on-prem deployments, the provider will provide a documented procedure and a management tooling package to configure purge windows and confirm state.

4) Evidence and Auditability Requirements:
  - Logs: Provider will retain immutable operational logs necessary to prove that purge or eviction operations occurred. Logs must include timestamps, actor (service or admin id), tenant id, object identifiers, and action result.
  - Tamper evidence: audit logs must be write-once and cryptographically tamper-evident for a minimum of 90 days for hosted deployments.
  - Artifacts for customer review: upon request, within 10 business days, provider will produce an evidence package showing cache purge events and a checksum manifest of destroyed artifacts for the requested time window.

5) SLAs Related to Cache Behavior and Availability (operational commitments):
  - Availability of purge API: 99.9% monthly uptime.
  - Purge completion for targeted tenant cache (reasonable size thresholds): 95% of purge requests to complete within 5 minutes, 99.9% within 60 minutes. Large purge jobs (exceeding agreed size) may require staged/delete windows; these will be documented in the Order Form.
  - Consistency SLO: after purge completion, subsequent inference requests must not load purged KV entries (i.e., there must be no rehydration from persisted copies) in 99.99% of cases.

6) Incident Response and Forensics:
  - Notification: If residual data exposure is suspected, Provider will notify Customer within 24 hours of detection with initial impact scope and mitigation steps.
  - Forensics: Provider will preserve all relevant artifacts (logs, snapshots, config state) in a sealed evidence bundle for at least 90 days and make them available to Customer or an agreed independent auditor.
  - Root cause and remediation plan: Provider will deliver a technical incident report within 10 business days of initial notification and a remediation timeline.

7) On-Prem and VPC Specifics:
  - For private deployments where customer controls hardware or network: Provider will ship management tooling that automates cache purge and produces the same evidence artifacts described above; however, the customer retains control over physical access, and the provider’s obligations for uptime of purge APIs are limited to the management tooling being available and tested.
  - For air-gapped deployments, evidence collection procedures will be adapted to offline transfer methods; timelines may be extended by mutual agreement but must remain auditable.

8) Model Artifact and Provenance Requirements:
  - Provider shall include a model-provenance manifest for any model weights or tokenizer artifacts used in serving: model id, provider id, architecture, training-data provenance statement (high-level), and any license obligations.
  - If model replacement or fallback causes data to be routed to a different model artifact, Provider must record and make available a change log tied to request routing events for audit.

9) Limited Liability and Remedies (contract language suggestions):
  - In the event of confirmed residual data breach attributable to Provider negligence or misconfiguration, Provider liability shall include remediation assistance, cost of customer notification, and reasonable third-party audit fees up to the limits in the main agreement.
  - Provider will offer, as a commercially reasonable remedy, a one-time credit or remediation scope to address customer verification needs (e.g., independent re-audit).

Operational Checklist (what evidence we will be expected to produce during negotiations or audits):
- Per-tenant cache segregation evidence (config snapshots)
- Purge API call logs and completion timestamps
- Checksum manifest of destroyed/purged artifacts (or proof-of-deletion when persistent storage used)
- Immutable audit log extract for the requested window (sha256 fingerprints)
- Model provenance manifest and routing change log
- Sample management tooling runbook for private deployments

Appendix: Suggested Contract Snippets (copy/paste friendly)
1) Segregation: "Provider shall implement tenant-scoped caches and shall not use shared cache namespaces across customers. Provider will provide configuration export showing cache namespace per tenant upon request."

2) Purge API: "Provider will maintain an API to request immediate purge of a tenant’s caches. Provider commits to the purge completion SLA specified in this addendum and will provide an evidence package for completed purge operations within 10 business days."

3) Audit Evidence: "Provider will retain tamper-evident audit logs and produce an evidence bundle that demonstrates purge, eviction, and retention behavior for the period in question. Evidence delivery timelines and formats are specified in the Order Form."

Open Questions for Legal/Product Review (to be resolved prior to publication):
- Maximum acceptable TTL defaults across hosted, dedicated and private offerings (product needs guidance).
- Exact sizing thresholds for which purge SLAs degrade to staged deletion (engineering to propose).
- Whether cryptographic shredding (re-encryption with discarded keys) will be required for certain regulated customers.
- For on-prem customers, the acceptable window for evidence delivery if network or shipping logistics introduce delays.

Next Steps and Owner Actions:
- Security: validate required log schemas and tamper evidence implementation (owner: Daniel Kim).
- Product: propose default TTLs and UI controls for cache management (owner: Lina Moreno).
- Legal: review liability language and confirm limits align with DPA/MSA (owner: Omar Shah).
- Engineering: prototype per-tenant purge API and proof-of-deletion manifest generation (owner: Erik Voss).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally prescriptive to reduce negotiation cycles for inference-specific requests. It attempts to balance operational realism (fast ephemeral caches for latency) with customer controls and auditable proof to address compliance/regulatory concerns. Please comment inline with concrete alternatives for TTLs and SLA numbers rather than high-level objections; we will iterate to a pragmatic baseline that product/eng can implement.
